column1: # What the differential test compares, and where each file came from.
# Columns: role, source (commit:path, a release asset, or the path in this repo), sha256 of the bytes.
# The one published build is the rolling dev pre-release, 0.0.0-nightly.20260915.3a5666b, built
# from 3a5666b. There is no v* release and no predecessor repo. Configuration/PluginConfig.cs, the
# reader that build read the .cfg with, is the same file at 3a5666b and at 686aa7a, the commit the
# reader in src/ViewfinderHeadTracking/Legacy was frozen from, restructured to fill LegacyConfig and
# write nothing. It uses no core code. The oracle is that file byte for byte.
published reader
frozen from
oracle copy
frozen reader
frozen reader
frozen reader
BepInEx 6
# BepInEx 6.0.0-be.785. The test ran its BepInEx/core/BepInEx.Core.dll
# (sha256 352aacc2d5356489a00891f76db28b6463c81d25bcb02f90035171a669b7e35b), which the game loads.
# No published build shipped the plugin .cfg, in its ZIP or as a launcher-manifest.json seed (the dev
# installer ZIP, sha256 54b40aa757741d0c753d03cc99413890fa4306baf64de29473a689a9775b85fb, was listed to check),
# so the input is what the build writes at its first start: the .cfg the oracle, the published
# PluginConfig.cs byte for byte, writes when its Initialize runs on a ConfigFile at a path with no file
# and the plugin's BepInPlugin metadata (GUID, name and version 0.0.0), as BasePlugin builds it. It ran
# on .NET 8 with that BepInEx.Core.dll and the UnityEngine.CoreModule of the UnityEngine.Modules 2021.3.45
# package the plugin is built against. The "Acceptable values" comment lines list whichever KeyCode enum
# the harness loaded; in game they list the one the game's interop assemblies hold. No reader reads a
# comment line.
